title: a16z Podcast: Seeing into the Future -- Making Decisions, Telling Stories

reader_summary.source_label: From the episode notes — transcript not yet available
reader_summary.headline: with Steven Johnson (@stevenbjohnson), Chris Dixon (@cdixon).
reader_summary.overview: with Steven Johnson (@stevenbjohnson), Chris Dixon (@cdixon), and Sonal Chokshi (@smc90) There's a lot of research and writing out there on "thinking fast" -- the short-term, gut. Because we're not only talking about decisions like who to marry (or whether to move) here. why bother, if these decisions are so complex, with competing value systems, countless interacting variables, and unforeseeable second- and third-order effects?

key_points.text: Because we're not only talking about decisions like who to marry (or whether to move) here.
We can't predict the future, so why try?
